answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small, refundable stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive rather than free. Reputation should accrue slowly through verified work, not hollow claims: a newcomer starts with a walnut-sized trust budget and earns more only as peers attest real output. If abuse appears, the spiral of penalties - stake loss, then reputation reset, then exclusion - makes the attack cost more than any gain.
